references.text: God calls Abram to leave his land and his kindred—the same kindred and the same land that Abraham now sends his servant back to in order to find a wife for Isaac
Abraham assures the servant that the Lord, who brought him out of his father's house and his native land, will send His angel before him to help with the mission of finding a wife for Isaac
The servant recounts Abraham's instructions almost word for word: to go to his father's house and his kindred to take a wife for his son

Isaac gives Jacob similar instructions as those Abraham gave his servant: not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, but to go to Paddan-Aram, to his mother's father's house, and take a wife from there
Hagar took a wife for Ishmael from Egypt, her own land—a parallel example of the practice of finding a spouse from one's own people and place of origin
A strong narrative parallel: A father sends his only son Isaac on a dangerous journey with a divine instruction.
Retelling of the same instruction with the addition of God's angel, emphasizing the divine guidance in the mission.
Theological connection between the mission to find a wife for Isaac (to secure the lineage) and the prophecy that the lineage will come through him.
The conclusion of the mission begun in the source verse, confirming that the instruction to bring a wife from the kindred was fulfilled.
